deviations.claim_in_article: “They enjoyed AI’s convenience, but a human was on the other end. They did not realize it.”
deviations.issue: The article states as fact that users enjoyed the AI service and did not realize a human was making the call. The Ledger confirms that the test began without appropriate disclosure, but does not report users’ actual awareness or experience. The nearby conditional wording does not qualify this categorical statement.
deviations.explanation: The claim about users’ actual reactions and awareness is not established by the Ledger; presenting it categorically changes certainty and adds unsupported facts. The Ledger’s lack-of-disclosure finding does not establish that users did not realize it.
deviations.qualifier_text: “might think”; “If no one explained this clearly”

deviations.claim_in_article: “It said human staff made inappropriate comments about race during calls. These calls were about trying to lower internet or cable fees.”
deviations.issue: “These calls” describes multiple calls, whereas the Ledger records one reported case involving an internet or cable fee negotiation. The nearby references to one employee’s report do not undo the plural claim.
deviations.explanation: The plural wording expands the Ledger’s one reported case to multiple calls, changing both the number and the scope of the claim. The article’s one-report qualifier does not remove that plural assertion.
deviations.qualifier_text: “one employee’s report”; “only one report”; “wrong to say all contract workers did this”
